meta.phase-name: Canonical Content Accessors And Stat-Surface Normalization

phase-plan.purpose: Move gameplay/runtime code onto a single canonical content access layer, keep engine-owned stat language aligned around stat domains instead of trait/feature split terms, and make `contracts/index.ts` the obvious import surface for `LIST` / `BY_ID` / `BY_KEY` access instead of repeated local lookup maps.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: convenient collection accessor exports in `contracts/index.ts`; migration of `game.ts` away from local spell/rune/action lookup maps; documentation of canonical asset/access conventions; runtime-owned test fixtures updated from `traitDelta` naming where the runtime surface changed. Out of scope: full history/event payload renaming, full automated accessor codegen, and the event/progression/history extraction planned in 62-03.

file.description: Canonical normalized pack export surface; now also the home for stable collection accessors and lookup records.
Main engine composition root; should consume contract accessors instead of rebuilding local maps for spells, runes, and action metadata.
Architecture/reference doc that should explain canonical asset layers, naming conventions, editor-vs-runtime roles, and the current workflow.
Fixture coverage for runtime item payload naming; should track `narrativeStatDelta` where the runtime surface changed.
Presenter-side fixture coverage for runtime item payload naming.

task.description: Add canonical `LIST` / `BY_ID` / `BY_KEY` style exports for the important stat, spell, rune, item, quest, event, and action collections in `contracts/index.ts`.
Move `game.ts` off local spell/rune/action lookup maps and onto the canonical accessor layer so the file is more composition and less content-access boilerplate.

Finish the remaining runtime-owned naming/documentation cleanup: keep docs aligned, update lingering runtime-facing fixtures from `traitDelta` to `narrativeStatDelta`, and decide what should become true codegen instead of manual accessor exports.

decision.summary: `contracts/index.ts` is the canonical access surface for gameplay code, not just a bag of raw pack documents.
decision.impact: Gameplay code can import stable `LIST` / `BY_ID` / `BY_KEY` accessors instead of rebuilding local lookup maps and repeating pack-specific boilerplate.

decision.summary: The docs-site/Payload system remains editorial infrastructure while the game consumes published contract JSON and generated code artifacts.
decision.impact: `GAME_STRUCTURE.md` and future editor work should keep that boundary explicit so the runtime does not drift toward direct DB-row consumption.
